title: Volume 1 Chapter 3: To You Who Are Surprisingly Close, and to You Who Feel Breathtakingly Far Away 2
content: The most troublesome thing was that a group that seemed likely to interfere with our usual path was joining us.
From the perspective of adventurers, members of the church are specialists in healing magic. Normally, they are appreciated rather than disliked.
However, we were nobles, and we were just as skilled in healing magic as the church members.

After all, healing magic is essential for nobles. Being able to use healing magic significantly reduces the chances of being poisoned or assassinated, so nobles are taught healing magic from a young age.
Moreover, Erika was someone who had been told by the church to die, as she was accused of attempting to assassinate the Light Priestess. This was far too much of an unwanted favor.
"That's... a very kind offer," I said, surprised as I looked at Erika.
"We were just discussing how we should raise our adventurer rank," she replied.

Right? I nodded back at her, as if to confirm her statement. It was impressive that Erika, being a high noble's daughter, could keep quiet about money and all the church-related matters, but what was her intention?
Regarding the money, it was likely a matter of consideration, thinking the other party would be concerned. But the other party was a church sister, one of those who told her to die!
"If Sister Shara is going to join us, that would be a great help," Erika continued.
"Just call me Shara, my lady," Shara replied.
"Then please refer to me as Erika."
Shara seemed relieved to have been accepted so easily, and Erika spoke cheerfully. How could she converse so amicably with the church members?
To me, the church was made up of those who had taken away her brilliant future.
"Um, Erika? Your husband looks like he’s making a strange face. Did I do something wrong?" Shara asked quietly.
"Don't worry about it. He’s probably just thinking about something complicated," Erika reassured her.
"Shin—" Erika called my name, pulling me out of my thoughts.

"You don’t need to think so hard that you make that face, you know? After all, the church has been very kind to my best friend. The church is the protector of my dear friend. So there’s no need for you to worry so much."
Was her concern about Erika's own feelings? Even so... ah, no, Erika said it was fine.
I took a deep breath to calm myself. Alright, I was calm now.
"If you say so, then I guess I don’t need to think too much about it anyway," I said, trying to laugh it off and shrug.
"My name is Shin Longdagger. I look forward to working with you."
I said this to Shara, who looked confused.
"So, what were you two planning to do today?" Shara asked, her curiosity piqued as we entered the Adventurer Guild building.
The early morning Adventurer Guild was bustling with adventurers looking for work, lively and noisy.
"I need a bit of money, so I was thinking of looking for a good quest," I replied, glancing at the quest board. Shara responded with a casual "Oh," as if it were someone else's business.
She had mentioned earlier that she was worried about being turned down, so perhaps she was relieved to be joining us after all.

"You two can run into money troubles too, huh?" she remarked, and as I nodded vaguely, Erika approached with a quest paper in hand. In that moment, I struggled to keep my face from contorting. The quest paper Erika brought was bordered in a sickly yellow and black stripe, unlike the others.
"Shin, I found something that looks good!" Erika said excitedly, as if she were asking for praise. Did she know what she was holding? No, she probably didn’t.
As Erika eagerly showed me the quest paper, I debated whether I should tell her what it was when a voice came from behind.
"Oh? If it isn’t Mr. Longdagger," it was Lana, a guild staff member. She noticed the quest paper in Erika's hand and kindly warned her.
"Be very careful with that one. The striped border essentially means 'stay away.' It’s a dangerous area, and there’s really no point in taking on that quest."
She explained that it was a story unrelated to us, but foolish adventurers often take on reckless challenges for the sake of the reward.
Sorry, but unfortunately, we were leaning towards the foolish side right now.
Erika seemed intrigued by Lana's words, and I thought, ah, this is settled. There would be no hesitation for Erika, who was determined to uphold her noble face.
Behind Erika, Shara was curiously looking over the quest board. Is it really okay, Shara? Your fate seems to be decided here.
"Wow, there are so many people troubled by monsters," she remarked, but was this really the time to be impressed?
"By the way, how much is the reward for that quest?" Erika asked, her tone as casual as if she were asking for the price of bread. The contrast with the quest paper in her hand was striking.
"The magic stone is definitely going to auction, but combined with the subjugation reward, it should be enough to buy a nice mansion," Lana replied.
Yes, it was confirmed. Our fates were now decided.
"Even if we can buy a house, it won’t mean anything if we die," I said, jokingly laughing as I watched Lana and Erika exchange smiles, with Erika replying, "That’s absolutely true."
I made a mental note to at least not die.

"So, what are you two planning to do today? A quest? A skirmish?" Shara asked as we reached the edge of the magic realm, in the first layer known as the grassland area. The magic realm can be roughly divided into three layers: the grassland area closest to human territory, the forest area further in, and the deep area even deeper within.
Although it was divided into three layers, we hadn’t even explored the forest area, so it was practically two layers.
By the way, Shara's mention of a skirmish referred to the act of adventurers hunting suitable monsters to earn their daily bread.
It seemed she had been looking for something in the guild, but with a carefree attitude, she tilted her head, unaware of what she was about to do. Sorry, Shara, your fate has already been decided.
"I found a very good quest at the guild, so I think I’ll aim for that today," I said.
Instead of saying I would "take" the quest, I said I would "aim" for it, which would raise alarms for any ordinary adventurer.
"Let’s hunt the designated subjugation target today. A dragon."
"Huh?"
Shara looked at me as if I had just said pigs would fall from the sky tomorrow, at the casual mention of "dragon," as if it were as normal as saying the weather was clear today.
"By the way, it’s a Forest Dragon."
"That’s not just a casual mention, is it?!"
Shara grabbed my collar and shook me vigorously. I was just trying to be helpful, and yet this was how I was treated.
"It’s a dragon!? Why are you so calm about this?!"
"Isn’t it great? Your first job is a dragon!"
Where is the good point in that? Shara shook me three times with great force.
Behind us, Erika wore a face that seemed to ask why there was any need to panic.
I hadn’t mentioned it, but Shara looked like a sinner confessing her crimes.
"Um, I’m a sister, but I’m not very good at healing magic, you see..."
She pleaded with her gaze, as if to say, "It’s impossible to hunt a dragon with a sister like me."
"I know."
"I know," both Erika and I replied, thinking, what’s with the sudden concern?
"I’ve seen you struggle to heal even a wound where ribs were sticking out."
Shara looked at Erika with a face that seemed to say, "That’s not something to worry about."
Still unwilling to give up, Shara waved her hands and continued, "I’m so bad at healing magic that I was told to change factions!"
"Change factions, you say?"
Erika tilted her head, likely unfamiliar with the church's factions. But still, her gestures were so cute.

"I was originally part of the healing faction, but... as a sister, I ended up being better at attack magic than healing magic, and I was told by my seniors and the bishop that I should change factions."
"I'm sorry, I thought if I said this, you wouldn’t let me join the party," Shara apologized.

The healing faction she mentioned is a group within the church that primarily focuses on healing people with healing magic, while the faction that accompanies adventurers to hunt monsters is called the Protectorate Subjugation faction.
Seeing Shara looking so downcast, I realized this was more than I had expected. It seemed she hadn’t wanted to change factions, so in essence, she had been expelled from her faction.
"People have their strengths and weaknesses, so it’s best not to worry too much," I said.
See? This is why it’s impossible to go dragon hunting with a sister like her, Shara insisted with her gaze, but Erika spoke to her gently.
"You’re more suited to this now, Shara, who tried to face the Golden Ogre for the sake of the villagers, despite being injured."

Erika’s words were meant to comfort her, but for someone from the former healing faction who aimed to save the weak through healing, it wouldn’t be comforting at all. What Shara really wanted to hear was probably a promise to stop the dragon hunt.
"Is that so?" Shara said, her expression unexpectedly brightening.
"Yes, indeed. I can’t imagine you using healing magic in a clinic while trying to face strong enemies for the sake of the weak."
Shara laughed, but I couldn’t help but think back to how she was the type to choose to fight even when her ribs were sticking out.
In other words, she was more of an adventurer.
"Do you think I can do it?" she asked.
"I’ll guarantee it; you can do it, Shara," Erika replied.
"I’ll do my best!" Shara said cheerfully, and Erika smiled with satisfaction.
Is it really okay, Shara? You’re going to hunt a dragon now, you know? Perhaps my doubts showed in my gaze, as Shara noticed and paused for a moment before shouting.
"No! But a dragon is too much!"
Her shout was ignored.
"Are you serious?"
At this point, Shara’s face had turned pale.
"Yes, I’m serious."
Shara looked at me as if seeking help, but I shrugged and ignored her. She was being so stubborn; she should remember when her ribs were sticking out.
"It’s a designated subjugation target, a dragon, you know?"
She looked at me as if checking my sanity.

By the way, a designated subjugation target refers to a monster specified by the Adventurer Guild. It’s commonly called a "master" because most monsters have a general habitat in this area, but designated subjugation targets are those that have wandered in from other regions and settled here.
They act as if they are asserting their territory, hence the title of "master."
These monsters are capable of displacing others, so they tend to be more dangerous and stronger than regular individuals.

Despite this, they usually don’t move from the area they’ve settled in, so the guild posts them as permanent quests, not so much to demand their subjugation as to warn underqualified adventurers to stay away.
In other words, we were going to hunt a monster we didn’t need to kill for the sake of money. Truly adventurer-like.
"According to the quest paper, the target is a Forest Dragon. It’s a bit careless of them to establish their territory in the grassland, despite being called a forest dragon."
"That careless one is normally a monster the knight order would deal with, you know?!"
Shara couldn’t help but shout at Erika for treating a dragon so lightly.
"Is that so?"
"How should I know? The knight order doesn’t usually respond to Forest Dragons in Faltarl!"
When I answered Erika's question, Shara exclaimed that Faltarl was too much of a magic realm! It wasn’t that bad, though it was certainly a magic realm, except for my master.
"You don’t need to worry so much. I’m here, and Shin is here. If it gets dangerous, we can just run away."
"I really don’t want to play tag with my life!"

As Shara shouted loudly, Erika laughed cheerfully. Perhaps it was refreshing and enjoyable for her to see someone express their emotions so openly, as there hadn’t been anyone like that at the academy.
If Shara, the sister, could make Erika smile like this, then I could tolerate her being around. But I was still annoyed at being interrupted when it was just the two of us.
"Oh, we’ve arrived."
Shara muttered with a face that looked like she might cry. Ahead, we could see the Forest Dragon lounging on a low hill.
"It’s big," Erika remarked succinctly, and I replied that it was indeed a bit large.
"It’s too big!"
Are we really going to take down a dragon as big as a house just to earn a down payment? I see, that makes sense.
"Shall we take a shot at it?"
Erika’s voice was devoid of tension, while Shara’s voice, shouting "Don’t ignore me!" was filled with despair.
"I’ll be the vanguard, right?"
"Yes, I’ll provide support from a distance, and Shara will cast attack magic from the rear. Let’s try that formation for now."
"Well, if we’re just going to take a light shot, that should be fine. What if we can take it down right away?"
"I’m not very familiar with fighting monsters. Shin, what would you do?"
"Leaving it half-injured and then trying again is a foolish strategy. It’s either take it down or retreat."
"Then I’ll leave that judgment to you, the vanguard."
"Got it. Now, let’s check your firepower."
When I looked over at Shara, she was completely dazed.
"Shara, snap out of it. I want to check your firepower."
"Huh? My firepower?"
"Yes, how much is your maximum firepower?"
"I don’t have much firepower with regular magic, but if I can use syllable magic, it should be decent."
I see, Shara was a user of syllable magic. Syllable magic requires a special vocalization method to cast spells and is also known as chant magic, which is a rare form of magic.

It’s simply difficult to use. You have to memorize the syllabic magic circles called spells and practice the special vocalization method, which is a high hurdle to overcome. As a downside, it takes time to activate, making it unpopular among adventurers.
However, its power is nothing short of incredible. It’s a type of magic more commonly used by knight orders than by adventurers. It’s also known as destruction magic.
I remembered how she often referred to herself as part of the healing faction. Was she really the only one who used chant magic in that faction? But well...
"That means it should be sufficient even against a dragon. Let’s aim to take a shot at that first."
Erika and I made final checks on our equipment, tightening our sword belts and checking the fastenings on our armor.
"How long does it take for your magic to activate, Shara?"
"If it’s my maximum firepower, it takes at least three minutes at the fastest. See? It’s impossible, right? Three minutes against a dragon? Let’s go home, okay?"

Even the weakest known magic can penetrate a dragon’s scales. I didn’t know how skilled Shara was with her syllable magic, but three minutes for her fastest spell was already in the realm of experienced users.
That was a pleasant surprise; I had been prepared to fight the dragon for at least five to ten minutes.
"Three minutes is fine. What about you, Erika?"
"I just need to stand between Shin and Shara for three minutes and stop the dragon’s attacks, right?"
Erika smiled.
"That’s an ‘easy win’ then."
Erika concluded the preparations with words typical of an adventurer.
"Where does that confidence come from...?" Shara glared at Erika with tearful eyes, as if pleading.
I looked at Erika’s face. Her golden magic power sparkled beautifully.
"Because Erika is behind me."
"Because Shin is in front of me."
The overlapping voices made me feel a bit embarrassed.
"Stop bragging in this situation!" Shara shouted.
So fast! Too fast!
Shara, who was being carried like a package by Erika, shouted this, while Erika gently warned her to be careful.

Since Shara’s body enhancement was weaker than ours, she had to be carried by Erika to match our pace, but Erika was keeping up without any delay. Shara, being carried, was complaining, but she had rejected the idea of going ahead alone, so she had to endure it.
The Forest Dragon, lounging on the hill, must have noticed our approach, but it showed no reaction. It was impressive how it could be called a master.
But it was also overly complacent.
As we closed the distance to about a hundred feet, I drew my sword and increased the intensity of my body enhancement.
As I accelerated, Shara shouted from behind, "Charging straight at that thing is insane!"

Anyone with sanity wouldn’t become an adventurer, nor would they think of taking down a dragon the size of a house for a down payment. I had thrown away my sanity the moment I was chosen for elopement. I could do anything for Erika!
I charged forward with all my strength.

The Forest Dragon was called that because it lived in the forest, which is a common misconception. In reality, it was simply because its skin resembled wood and it had spikes on its back that looked like a small forest.
The green organs resembling leaves on the spikes rustled in the wind.
I looked down at it while preparing my sword.
The iron rule of monster subjugation: always take the initiative when you can. Following that lesson, I jumped high to take the Forest Dragon by surprise.
The moment I stomped down hard on the ground, the Forest Dragon seemed to lose track of me and looked around in confusion for the first time.
No, no, that’s too slow. Way too slow.
As the Forest Dragon finally noticed me above it and raised its head to bite, I swung down my sword.
A dull thud echoed, one that hardly sounded like a sword cutting through flesh.
The Forest Dragon’s head, forced to close its mouth as it tried to bite, slammed into the ground and bounced back.
As I landed, I was amazed by the feel of my sword.

What was great was that I could adjust the sharpness. I had learned this from Tepe, the weapon shop owner, but I was impressed all over again. Moreover, I didn’t have to worry about it breaking at all. I didn’t even feel anxious about slamming it against the Forest Dragon’s tough hide.
Checking behind me, I saw Erika and Shara had taken their positions.
About twenty feet away was the distance determined to ensure Shara’s maximum firepower would hit. For us, without a shield, this was a bit too close against the Forest Dragon.
But Erika stood in front of Shara, so there was no need to worry.
"Whoa."
I took a light step back as a foreleg the size of my height passed right in front of me.
The Forest Dragon glared at me with eyes filled with hatred. Its nostrils flared, and it seemed quite angry.
"Good, keep focusing on me."
As I heard Shara’s incantation from behind, I slowly moved to the side.
The Forest Dragon’s head turned toward me, as if drawn in.
Ah, good.
I stomped down hard on the ground again. I certainly didn’t intend to fight it head-on.

I moved to the side of the Forest Dragon and slammed my sword into its side, which shouldn’t have been possible for a creature. The Forest Dragon seemed to lose track of me again, letting out a roar of agony as it flailed its body wildly in response to the sudden attack on its side.
I deflected the massive tail and foreleg attacks with my sword, keeping my body moving.
Its massive body was about the size of a small house, and even a little flailing was more than enough to create an impressive spectacle.

I slashed at its hind legs, increasing the sharpness of my sword in case I needed to escape, and struck other areas with my sword like a blunt weapon, making sure to keep its focus on me and not let it settle on any one target.
